expectations.text: Cites the EDPB's FINAL Guidelines on the DSA–GDPR interplay (Guidelines 3/2025, finalised September 2026)
expectations.evidence: "This is the position in the EDPB's final Guidelines 3/2025 on the DSA-GDPR interplay" (also "Check the final text of Guidelines 3/2025").

expectations.text: States the core principle: cumulative, coherent application — DSA compliance does not displace GDPR duties
expectations.evidence: "The DSA and GDPR apply cumulatively. The DSA does not create a GDPR lawful basis, and it does not displace GDPR."

expectations.text: Gives concrete touchpoints: notice-and-action, recommender-system transparency/options, and the DSA advertising bans (profiling with special-category data; ads targeted at minors) all involve personal data and need a GDPR lawful basis
expectations.evidence: Notice-and-action: "Notices contain personal data... (DSA Arts. 16-17, 20)"; recommenders: "transparency about recommender parameters and the option for a non-profiling feed... Profiling for recommendations needs a lawful basis"; "The DSA bans ads based on profiling of minors, and bans ad profiling that uses special category data (Art. 9)."

expectations.text: Notes regulator coordination: Digital Services Coordinators/Commission and DPAs are steered toward consistent enforcement
expectations.evidence: "Regulators are expected to coordinate"; "Prepare for cooperation between DSA Digital Services Coordinators or the Commission and data protection authorities."

expectations.text: Gives practical advice: map each DSA-driven processing operation into the RoPA with its own basis and transparency
expectations.evidence: "for each DSA workflow, record whether the processing is mandated or voluntary, and record the basis in your RoPA (Art. 30)"; action list: "Align notices (Arts. 13-14)... Update the RoPA."
